brief.scope: Adversarial review of lane fix batch 1: the branch lane/lane-fixes against dev (origin/dev at 77f7c1a); the diff between them is the change under review and the contract (scope items 1 to 12 plus the plan) is in the input file, with the session's review notes appended. Judge the implementation against the contract's acceptance list: what is claimed green but not proven, what the tests let through (the wrapper's real launch path was proven only against an executable stub), what a tripped or resumed run would do on this tree, and what the dry-run JSON hides. Findings as quotation pairs with file and line, priority P1 to P3; opinions marked as such.

findings.claim: A tripped write is not committed (`if role == "write" and rec["harness"]["name"] == "codex" and residual and not tripped:`), `_resume` never calls `_settle` or `_commit_for_harness` and always `return 0` (launch.py:1403), and `collect` then refuses because `failed = bool(last.get("tripped") or last.get("exit"))` is false after a successful resume (launch.py:1429-1436: "let a normal finish settle itself"). A timeout close is envelope status `invalid`, so `_resume` also does `env.update(settled_refusal)` (launch.py:1390-1391) and land.py:169 still says "adjudicate the rejected dispatch by hand". A battery-trip resume can leave envelope `ok` with `refs/dispatch/<id>` still at the base, so land prints `landed n=0` and drops the residual. Watch tests never resume a tripped write: test_launch_watch.py has no `_settle` / `_commit_for_harness`.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; p=Path('ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py').read_text(); r=p.split('def _resume')[1].split('def _collect')[0]; c=p.split('def _collect')[1].split('def _wait')[0]; assert '_settle(' not in r and '_commit_for_harness(' not in r and 'return 0' in r and 'settled_refusal' in r; assert 'let a normal finish settle itself' in c; print('resume-without-settle and collect-state after exit 0 confirmed')" && python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; t=Path('ops/devlane/dispatch/tests/test_launch_watch.py').read_text(); assert '_settle' not in t and '_commit_for_harness' not in t; print('watch tests do not pin settle on resume')"

findings.claim: The wrapper now execs `WF_AGENT=$agent "${argv[@]}"` instead of `python3 "${argv[@]}"`. Slice A proved that path only against `_plant_executable` sentinels (`path.chmod(... S_IXUSR)` at test_dispatch_wrapper.py:243-246). The only test that names the real sibling `launch.py` is dry-run (`test_conf_without_pin_resolves_the_sibling_launcher` at test_dispatch_wrapper.py:922). The 644/126 failure was fixed by hand in fdfbfd5 (mode-only; tree is now 100755) with no `os.access(launch.py, os.X_OK)` pin, so the suite stays green if the bit is lost.
findings.reproduce: stat -c '%a' ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py && git ls-files -s ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py && python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; w=Path('ops/conductor/tools/dispatch.sh').read_text(); assert 'python3 \"\${argv[@]}\"' not in w; assert 'WF_AGENT=\$agent \"\${argv[@]}\"' in w; t=Path('ops/conductor/tests/test_dispatch_wrapper.py').read_text(); assert 'os.access(path, os.X_OK)' in t and 'sentinel not executable' in t; assert 'os.access(sibling' not in t; print('exec-without-python3; tests pin sentinel +x only')"

findings.claim: Dry-run JSON is `{"argv", "env", "launcher"}` where `env` is only `WF_AGENT` and optional `DISPATCH_TIMEOUT`. It does not say argv[0] is exec'd (no python3), and it has no `--detach`, `DETACH_WAIT`, or jobs-root field. `print_launch` then `((dry_run)) && exit 0` (dispatch.sh:198-199) runs before the detach branch, so `--dry-run --detach` is a foreground plan. That is what hid the interpreter change that produced exit 126.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; s=Path('ops/conductor/tools/dispatch.sh').read_text().splitlines(); assert s[197]=='print_launch' and s[198]=='((dry_run)) && exit 0'; body='\n'.join(s[183:189]); assert 'DISPATCH_TIMEOUT' in body and 'WF_AGENT' in body; assert 'detach' not in body.lower(); assert 'python3' in body and 'sys.argv[3:]' in body; print('dry-run JSON is env-subset and precedes detach')"

findings.claim: Plan 3.10 required `review_pages`, `buckets`, and `expected_checks` under one try. Only `buckets` is caught (`try:` at pr_overview.py:498). `review_pages` still raises `Unavailable` and `main` exits 2 with no rows — the same board-wide refusal defect 10 named, for a different per-PR read. Tests inject only `check_errors` (test_collect_rows.py:287-314) and `.claude/skills/pr-overview/tests` is absent from `ops/bin/suites.sh:17`.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; p=Path('.claude/skills/pr-overview/pr_overview.py').read_text().splitlines(); loop='\n'.join(p[491:530]); assert 'review_pages' in loop and loop.find('review_pages') < loop.find('try:'); assert 'unreadable_checks' in loop; s=Path('ops/bin/suites.sh').read_text(); assert 'pr-overview' not in s; t=Path('.claude/skills/pr-overview/tests/test_collect_rows.py').read_text(); assert 'check_errors' in t and 'review_pages' not in t.split('def run_board')[1].split('def test_')[0]; print('review_pages unwrapped; suite omits pr-overview tests')"

findings.claim: `envelope-status` needed text is still "adjudicate the rejected dispatch by hand; the lever lands only accepted work", against acceptance "lands through the lever, never by hand" and plan 3.12, which required this refusal to name `launch.py collect`. Collected trips skip the line; an uncollected invalid envelope with exit 0 still gets the by-hand instruction.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; t=Path('ops/conductor/tools/land.py').read_text(); assert 'adjudicate the rejected dispatch by hand' in t; idx=t.find('if env_status != \"ok\" and not collected:'); chunk=t[idx:idx+400]; assert 'launch.py collect' not in chunk; print('envelope-status needed remains by-hand')"

findings.claim: Opinion: `collect` walls verify with `timeout = float((rec.get("caps") or {}).get("timeout") or 900)` — the resolved wall of the run that already died — and has no flag to raise it. The plan's live proof `launch.py collect … --verify 'bash ops/bin/suites.sh'` cannot complete on a timeout-tripped implement. Tests lock the recorded wall in (`test_collect_verify_is_walled_by_the_job_cap_in_the_snapshot`).
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; c=Path('ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py').read_text().split('def _collect')[1].split('def _wait')[0]; assert 'rec.get(\"caps\")' in c and '--timeout' not in c; t=Path('ops/devlane/dispatch/tests/test_launch_collect.py').read_text(); assert 'test_collect_verify_is_walled_by_the_job_cap_in_the_snapshot' in t; print('collect verify wall is the recorded run cap')"

findings.claim: Opinion: `extend-exclude` gained `"../home"` so a repository lint file names a launcher-runtime sibling. From the repo root that path is a sibling of the git checkout, not a job directory; it only matches `job_dir/home` when ruff's project root is a dispatch snapshot. The session notes already asked reviewers about this.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; lines=Path('ruff.toml').read_text().splitlines(); assert lines[30].strip()=='\"../home\",'; assert 'launcher' in lines[29].lower() or 'launcher' in lines[28].lower(); print('ruff.toml excludes ../home')"

envelope.note: Judged lane/lane-fixes at 3ec08d1 against origin/dev 77f7c1a and the batch-1 contract (items 1-12 plus the plan). Inputs, timeout export, implement cap 3600, sibling launcher, schema append, spend fill, Claude argv permissions, collect-without-resume, and land-of-a-planted-collection are implemented and unit-pinned. CHANGES: a resumed tripped write cannot be collected or landed on this tree; the wrapper's real launch path and dry-run JSON do not pin exec-vs-python3 or detach; PR overview still refuses the board when review_pages fails and those tests are outside suites.sh.
